title.narrative: Sustaining safe water access through Integrated Water systems development and emergency support in Rural Tayeeglow, Bakool Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis nine-month WASH project proposed by SOVA will improve safe, equitable, and sustained access to drinking water for drought-affected rural communities in Tayeeglow District, Bakool Region, specifically Awgdheere, Qarsooy, Xawaal Kuule, El Garas, and Shimo. Tayeeglow continues to face severe WASH needs in 2025 due to prolonged drought, weak and non-functional water infrastructure, and recurring seasonal water shortages, exposing households to heightened public health risks and persistent exclusion from basic services. According to OCHA Somalia updates and inter-cluster analysis (2025), water availability in Tayeeglow remains critically constrained, with households relying on seasonal surface water, shallow wells, and berkads that often dry up or become unsafe, increasing reliance on costly and unsustainable water trucking. UNICEF WASH reports and WASH Cluster 4W data (2025) highlight limited chlorination, weak household water treatment, low sanitation coverage, and long distances to water points, heightening risks of waterborne disease and protection concerns, especially for women, girls, and children under five. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project responds to these challenges by addressing the core vulnerability of inadequate access to clean and reliable drinking water through an integrated WASH approach prioritising protection, inclusion, localisation, sustainability, and area-based coordination. It contributes to the WASH Cluster and HRP Strategic Objective SO2 (2025) and aims for at least 80 percent of households in the target villages to achieve sustained access to water that meets minimum humanitarian standards by project end. Key interventions include construction of three new shallow wells in Ceelgars and Shimo, rehabilitation of five existing shallow wells across the target villages, and development of two solar-powered borehole water supply systems in El Garas and Shimo, each equipped with elevated storage tanks, communal tap stands, and hydraulically isolated livestock troughs. To address acute gaps during peak dry periods, time-bound emergency water trucking will be implemented for two months in Awgdheere, Qarsooy, Xawaal Kuule, El Garas, and Shimo, alongside four rounds of routine water quality monitoring and testing. Sustainability will be reinforced through capacity building and ongoing support to Water Management Committees across all target villages.ltbrgtLocalisation and coordination are central to implementation. SOVA will leverage its established operational presence and community acceptance in Tayeeglow District, working through locally recruited WASH officers, technicians, and community-based structures. The project will converge geographically and programmatically with Health, Nutrition, and Food Security interventions implemented by MARDO, CRPD, SAMA, and CERID, ensuring households reached with WASH services also benefit from health outreach, nutrition services including GRRN fixed and outreach modalities, and food security assistance. Coordination will be maintained through WASH Cluster and Area-Based Coordination mechanisms, regular inter-agency meetings, timely 4W reporting, and joint analysis to ensure complementarity and avoid duplication, while complementing CERF, CBPF, and other donor-funded interventions.ltbrgtProtection will be systematically mainstreamed across all activities to ensure services are delivered in a safe, dignified, and inclusive manner. Through vulnerability-based targeting, transparent community validation, safe siting of infrastructure, and strong accountability mechanisms, the project will cumulatively reach 18,000 people at risk of exclusion, including 5,400 women, 4,500 girls, 4,500 boys, and 3,600 men. Accountability to Affected Populations will be strengthened through accessible complaints and feedback mechanisms, five gatekeeper agreements with mandatory PSEA clauses, inclusive community committees, and IEC messaging on entitlements and reporting pathways. ltbrgtlt/pgt
